screen.title: Cinema screen surface
notes: Only the physical surface is restored. The theatre screen has no runtime artwork or behaviour (checked in components/corridor); the corridor side screens (corridor-screens.tsx) are untouched.

floor-slab.title: Foundation floor slab
notes: Visible mostly in the front aisle between the stage and the first terrace.
limitations: Honed basalt has soft reflections; they are frozen as seen from the opening camera and will not slide with camera movement.
Close-up outliers sit on the stage/seat silhouettes (excluded runtime seats differ from Blender seats).

terraces.title: Terraces, aisles and treads (smoked walnut)
notes: One object holding all five terraces, aisles and treads; 128 overlapping projections were split into separate charts.
12 differently triangulated slivers matched to the nearest runtime triangle (within 32 mm, max 1% allowed).
limitations: Texel size is 15.7 mm (63.5 texels/m) to keep the atlas at 2048x4096; walnut grain is softer than Blender in very close orbit views. Much of the tread area is hidden under seating.
Outliers sit on seat silhouettes and the aisle edge reveals.

step-nosings.title: Stair nosings and aisle edge reveals
notes: 27 satin nickel step nosings plus four satin graphite inlaid aisle edge reveals. Both materials are fully metallic and use Object coordinates, so objects are baked unjoined.
Thin strips keep at least 16 texels across (anisotropic charts).
limitations: Fully metallic thin rims: Blender shows a narrow specular highlight along the aisle edge reveals that the frozen bake loses after texture filtering at grazing angles, so the reveals read darker (detail pose R3F 49 vs Blender 72 mean over the mask; the horizontal nosings match closely). Not fixable by more texels; it is view-dependent, and a second view-direction bake is not allowed.
Front-of-room views show the riser faces from the side the opening camera never sees.
step-nosings.status: Agent-verified with a known limitation (dark edge-reveal rims) — awaiting user review.

acoustic-slats.title: Lower reeded ash acoustic slats
notes: 308 reeded ash slats. The material reads per-object data (Object coordinates), so objects are baked unjoined (308 passes, about 2 hours on this machine); joining would change the per-slat grain.
At least 12 texels across each slat face; 4 px padding (8 px gutters).
limitations: From the opening eye the slats are mostly hidden by the runtime seats (taller than Blender's), hence the many outliers; the low aisle pose (off the bake eye) is the most useful view: RMSE 3.9 excluding outliers.

projector-floor.title: Projector floor / platform (PROJECTOR FLOOR | Original = source Second_floor)
notes: Target confirmed: runtime public/models/projector-floor-marked.glb node "projector-floor" (12 triangles, one box, no UVs) = layout object PROJECTOR FLOOR | Original = source object Second_floor in Theatre_Moon_Projector_optimized.blend (extract_native_floor.py + build_layout.py apply only the theatre translation (0.010995,-26,0.02)). Runtime bounds minus that translation equal Second_floor to 0.1 mm; every bake triangle matched within 0.002 mm.

Intended material: FLOOR V3 | Satin walnut PBR (object-linked slot; identical in the older live scene). Wood.117/Wood.003 in the native-world file and the corridor preparation are the unused data-level material underneath and were not used.

In the source, Second_floor and the whole projector are hidden from render and the floor's dedicated light (CINE | Projector hero key, LL | second floor only) has 0 energy. Only the floor is un-hidden, only in the disposable copy, for the bake and the matching Blender reference; no light was changed or added, and the projector (animated at runtime) casts no frozen shadow.

Runtime: the diagnostic node is hidden in the theatre route's own clone and a world-space copy is drawn with the baked atlas (components/corridor/baked-surfaces.tsx, extractNodeSurfaces). Projector code, materials, particles and controls untouched.

Single bake direction chosen by evidence: Blender replays of four candidate single bakes (wide, returned and close eyes; above-surface) were scored at all three journey views; the returned-view eye gave the lowest mean and worst-case error. Final result is ONE bake.
limitations: Satin walnut sheen is view-dependent and frozen from the returned view: from the wide approach the deck reads darker than Blender (RMSE 6.1) and from the close high view brighter (RMSE 9.3); the returned view matches (RMSE 1.6).
For these comparisons the runtime projector was hidden temporarily (capture-only) because the source render hides it; the deck under the projector is therefore compared without it.

moon-steel-border.title: Moon designs: polished steel border rings
notes: Included objects (exactly four, all "design moon"): Cylinder.018, Cylinder.020 (left wall), Cylinder.024, Cylinder.026 (right wall); 212 runtime triangles each, 848 total. Each is an annular steel ring 1.63-2.35 m from its moon centre; no modifiers.

All four use the same material, MOON | Polished stainless steel - fine polish (4 users): metallic 1.0, roughness 0.09-0.15 from world-position micro-polish noise, bump, and planar/edge normal blending. Excluded: mirror discs (OPT | ... baked angle reflections), Material.005 parts, White plastic and material-less moon parts, walls, speakers and fixtures.

Fixed 6144x6144 atlas (user requirement): 1,053 texels/m (about 0.95 mm), 83.2% used; every ring has its own charts (112 charts, ring backs facing the wall at 1/8 density), at least 16 texels across thin rims, 8 px padding. 4 objects joined into 2 bake passes (no per-object material inputs).

Bake viewpoint chosen by evidence: Blender replays of three single-eye candidates scored at four journey views (RMSE opening/closeup/detail/projector): opening eye 17.2/13.6/4.9/25.4 (mean 15.3), mid-pullback 20.6/42.7/46.9/62.1, projector side 21.0/33.7/59.4/8.4. The opening eye was kept; one active bake.

KTX2: UASTC level 3, RDO 0.25, sRGB DFD, box mips stopped at 12x12 (10 levels: 6144 to 12) so every level stays 4x4-block aligned for WebGL compressed formats; three.js allocates exactly the provided levels. The 6K authoring bake (EXR and 16-bit display PNG) is kept outside public.
Change check: diffing the opening view before/after this item, all changed pixels lie on the ring perimeters (within a few px); nothing else changed.
limitations: Mirror-polished steel is the most view-dependent material in the room: reflections are frozen as seen from the opening camera. From other angles they do not move; e.g. the off-axis view of a right ring reads cooler than Blender (RMSE 10.7 excluding outliers, blue channel 71 vs 41).

At normal framing the rings are 2-4 px wide; most masked error comes from the ring inner edge where Blender antialiasing blends the bright adjacent mirror glow while the site blends the still-diagnostic mirror. The ring itself matches at the 8 deg detail view (RMSE 3.3 excluding outliers).

Download 12.4 MB and about 48 MiB of GPU memory for this one texture (estimate for BC7/ASTC); devices without BC7/ASTC/ETC2 support would fall back to uncompressed RGBA (about 4x). This is the cost of the requested 6K runtime atlas.
